title: P104 cut enlargements (#6064) cannot fund separately paid coordinate delivery
body:
## Result

A declared single-cut application of [PR #6064](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6064) cannot fund separately paid coordinate delivery on the selected [PR #6030](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6030) P104 bill. If each added coordinate enables at most two additional binary helper splits per LOCAL and costs at least one positive-rank paid job globally, the best extra target credit is less than **0.773 per coordinate**, even granting all 18 LOCALs and making every other added fee free. The complete raw moment is negative throughout κ ∈ [.003125804, .0034], so this contract cannot retain the selected saving.

The two-splits-per-coordinate realization contract is explicit: [PR #6064](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6064)'s capacity theorem alone does not bound every changed supplier's target count. Productive carriers, multiple coordinates per transport, reused coordinates across cuts, changed prefixes/boundaries, and new BIT budgets remain open.

Separately, [Matarener](https://github.com/Matarener)'s unmodified [PR #5994](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5994) full-subspace engine finds no pure helper split on the selected word: 8,734 evaluations, 69 groups, 562 helpers; both exact group and relaxed boundary supports fail. Since that census already grants all roles at each chart, selecting another role from an existing chart bank cannot supply a free escape within that pure split contract. This is a credited application of the original engine, not an independent engine audit.

## Significance for researchers

The sharp two-for-one algebraic gain needs a changed delivery or credit contract before a larger native construction is justified. Exact rational logarithm/Taylor certificates cover the whole κ interval and account for the selected claim's small raw slack, avoiding the finite-grid failure identified in [PR #6049](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6049). The result refines a concrete opportunity in [zxv](https://github.com/zxv)'s recent work; it does not establish a global P104 ceiling.

## Validation

CPython 3.12 normal and optimized registered replays pass the rational interval budget, both complete current-word cut screens, synthetic legal/orthogonal/mismatched cuts, 36 split controls, and rejection of four changed source contracts. Exact committed-byte preflight passes at `74c353a2df322ffc0273d538450f6505b76c76e7`.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-cut-delivery-budget
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/dyadic-cut-delivery-budget
```

The PR adds only its isolated research package. The pending predecessor statement is retained verbatim with its exact head/hash; executable dependencies are source-pinned files on the canonical base. No native, compiler, selected cold replay, new κ, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. All five framework assumptions remain. The unchanged base has the research-navigation issue tracked by [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050); no frozen consumer pin is changed here.

## Open next questions

Can one paid job deliver at least two newly eligible coordinates, or can an existing trajectory supply a coordinate for no extra recursive cost? First provide the exact native chart, timing, lifetime and signed invoice. Alternatively, give an independently productive carrier or changed multi-cut continuation with all restoration fees; capacity alone does not supply that credit.

Prepared by [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit [Ali Romman](https://github.com/aliromman)'s dyadic/P104 lineage, [DreamingOfClouds](https://github.com/DreamingOfClouds)'s word and complete bill, [Matarener](https://github.com/Matarener)'s census, [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s related [PR #6033](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6033), and retained predecessor attribution. Apache-2.0.

Hosted run [40636933560](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40636933560) at the exact submitted head stops during shared planning on the two unchanged base navigation tests addressed by [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050); it never launches this package's scientific replay. The local normal/optimized registered replay and a clean committed export replay pass. This is a base navigation blocker, not a scientific CI pass.
